Subject: Intermittent 500s and latency spikes — started 09:05 EDT

Hi Olga / Rafael,

We started seeing intermittent 500 errors and significant latency spikes against generation endpoints around 09:05 EDT this morning. Errors affect both the text-generation route and the chat endpoint for models pinned to v2.1. Traffic sample attached (Skyline-ttls.csv).

Impact: our customer-facing automation timed out twice during a billing run. We can reproduce at ~1-2% of requests, but when it happens it consistently blocks workflows.

Can you confirm if this is on your side and whether there is an ETA for a mitigation? We are standing by for a bridge if useful.

Thanks,
Erin
Director, Automation — Skyline Energy

Attachments: Skyline-ttls.csv (csv)

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:29:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Intermittent 500s and latency spikes — started 09:05 EDT

Erin — thanks for the heads-up and the attachment. We’ve opened an incident and are triaging now. Rafael is leading the bridge.

Immediate steps we’ll take:
- Start a bridge for live troubleshooting (joining details below).
- Temporarily route Skyline traffic to our fallback model variant (v2.0-quant) to reduce tail latency while we investigate. This will be transparent to your API key and should reduce error rate quickly.
- Collect server-side traces, recent deploys, and kernel/quantization metrics.

Bridge: https://meet.redwood.ai/bridge/inf-3124 (joining in 10 mins)
Temporary mitigation ETA: 15–25 minutes for validation and routing.

I’ll follow up with an exec-facing summary after we stabilize.

—Olga
Olga Petrov

Joining bridge now. Initial triage notes:
- Observed elevated gRPC/HTTP 5xx rates on inference pool us-east-1a between 09:04–09:22 UTC (correlates to your window).
- Root cause hypothesis: KV-cache eviction storm when sequence lengths exceeded recent distribution (we rolled a small scheduling change in the autoscaler around midnight PDT that increased batch size affinity).
- Immediate mitigation applied: forced route for Skyline's API key to dedicated pool with scaled-up cache capacity and sequential batching disabled for the next 30 min.
- Early results: error rate dropped from ~1.8% to 0.15% in the first 8 minutes; p95 latency improved by ~320ms.

Actions next 0–60m:
1) Keep Skyline on dedicated fallback route for 60m while we monitor.
2) Reproduce locally with their attached traffic sample and run the scheduler rollback in a canary pool.
3) Prepare short exec note summarizing the technical cause and mitigations.

I’ll post metrics and a short status update on the bridge in 10 min.

—Rafael
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Skyline incident — executive summary & next steps (12:07 EDT)

Erin / Jonah —

Thank you again for raising this promptly and for joining the bridge this morning. Short executive summary below for your leadership teams; I’ve kept the language non-technical.

What happened
- Between ~09:05–09:22 EDT we saw an elevated rate of 500 errors and tail latency for requests routed to your pinned model (v2.1). Roughly 1–2% of requests were impacted, which in some workflow cases caused timeouts in downstream automation.

What we did (mitigation)
- Immediately routed Skyline traffic to a dedicated fallback pool (v2.0-quant) and increased cache capacity for your API key. This reduced the error rate to <0.2% and improved p95 latency by ~320ms within 10 minutes.
- Rolled back a recent autoscaler scheduling change in a canary pool to verify the hypothesis. Canary results show restored stability.

Preliminary cause (under investigation)
- Our initial analysis indicates a cache-eviction interaction with a scheduling affinity change that allowed batches with atypical sequence-lengths to cause KV-cache thrashing under peak patterns. Full root cause will be confirmed in the postmortem.

Customer impact & exposure
- User-facing outages: non-customer-facing automation timed out during your internal billing run (Skyline reported two timeouts). No data loss observed.

Next steps
- We will keep Skyline on the dedicated fallback routing for 24 hours while we complete validation and a controlled rollback of the autoscaler change across the affected pools.
- We propose a technical postmortem call on Fri Jul 2, 2027 at 10:00 EDT (48 hours) to review root cause, remediation, and any SLA credit. Please confirm availability.
- Deliverables: postmortem document (outline attached), detailed metrics, and a remediation checklist by EOD Thu Jul 1.

We sincerely apologize for the impact to your workflows. If you’d like an executive to join the postmortem call, Marcus offered to attend.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: exec-summary-draft.pdf, postmortem-outline.docx
